answer: A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 167 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The sable detector writes to anchor, and oasis reveals every merge. Submissions that land within 162 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 2 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
